title: How Ruben Hassid built a 78M-view LinkedIn audience: one platform, one persona, educational content
summary: Ruben Hassid explains how he grew from a music label to a top LinkedIn creator by focusing on a single platform and persona. He covers reverse-engineering what works, killing the ego, setting realistic expectations, and building problem-first rather than AI-first.

principles.text: Don't repurpose everywhere. Pick one platform and hammer it until you hit millions of views before expanding.
principles.quote: running more than one social media at high level is nearly impossible by by yourself I've I've seen very few people doing it you always have a team

principles.text: Write for one specific persona, and expect the persona to differ by platform.
principles.quote: when I'm creating Contents I keep writing for one person it's a known trick but I keep writing for one person

principles.text: Treat content like a startup product: use the fast feedback loop and track impressions as the core metric.
principles.quote: I take content and social media just like I would take like a product of a startup um you need to have feedback as fast as possible you need to Pivot with it

principles.text: Kill your ego: keep content purely educational rather than about your personal story.
principles.quote: if you look at my contents 99% of it uh it's just purely educational and I'm outside of it

principles.text: Before posting, spend days or weeks reverse-engineering what top creators in your niche do.
principles.quote: reverse engineer what's working and there's a high chance you're at least on the right path

principles.text: Posting is only a third of the game; the rest is commenting, DMs and networking on the platform.
principles.quote: content is a third and two third is commenting DM and the rest
